llm.summary: This skill is a coherent research workflow for assessing meta-analysis topics and generating local reports, with no evidence of hidden access, persistence, or unsafe execution.

dimensions.detail: The included Python script uses only the standard library, reads a user-supplied JSON file, and writes a specified Markdown or HTML report; no subprocess, network, credential, broad local indexing, or destructive behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is standard skill installation or manual copying into a skills directory; no post-install hooks, services, package dependencies, or remote payload execution were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to read bundled reference files, optionally use WebFetch for relevant research databases, and save report outputs; these are disclosed and purpose-aligned, though users should keep searches and outputs scoped to their project.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The only persistence is normal skill installation and user-directed report/example file creation; the script can overwrite the chosen output path, so users should choose output filenames carefully.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capabilities match the stated purpose: PICO decomposition, feasibility and novelty scoring, deduplication-search guidance, PRISMA/AMSTAR-2 checks, PROSPERO mapping, and Markdown/HTML report generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that the skill may guide web/database searches and create local report files from your research inputs. Use project-specific output paths, review any generated methodology recommendations, and treat rapid assessments as tentative until deduplication searches are completed.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The cited rapid-assessment trigger is somewhat natural-language, but it includes the domain term "meta" and appears in a list of meta-analysis examples, so it is not evidence of context hijacking or unrelated activation.
[LP3] expected: The skill does not declare a granular tool-permission scope, but the artifact text discloses the local reference reads, optional WebFetch use for PROSPERO/PubMed assistance, and report-file output; no broad or hidden local authority was found.
[SQP-3] expected: The language-scope items are methodology and localization concerns, not security concerns here; English/Chinese examples and non-English database guidance are visible and tied to evidence-coverage decisions rather than hidden behavior.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no results and a security score of 100; independent inspection likewise found no instruction hijacking, persistence, remote execution, tool spoofing, credential handling, or malicious code.
